HOME SCIENCE MARCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: HOME SCIENCE MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 100 °C

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Meals for Special Occasions? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Meals for Special Occasions.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Meals for Special Occasions.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Meals for Special Occasions.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Meals for Special Occasions.

3. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. newton (N)
   C. joule (J)
   D. watt (W)

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Consumer Protection? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Consumer Protection.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Consumer Protection.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Consumer Protection.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Consumer Protection.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Careers in Food and Nutrition? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Careers in Food and Nutrition.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Careers in Food and Nutrition.

6. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Producers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Yeast Products? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Yeast Products.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Yeast Products.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Yeast Products.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Yeast Products.

9. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Pastry Making? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pastry Making.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Pastry Making.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Pastry Making.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Pastry Making.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Special Treatment in Laundry Work? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Special Treatment in Laundry Work.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Special Treatment in Laundry Work.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Special Treatment in Laundry Work.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Special Treatment in Laundry Work.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Care of the Home: Exterior Environment? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Care of the Home: Exterior Environment.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Clothing Construction Processes: Collars 3.3 Clothing Construction Processes: Sl and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Clothing Construction Processes: Collars and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Clothing Construction Processes: Sleeves and Cuffs 3.4 Garment Design and Sketch and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Clothing Construction Processes: Sleeves and Cuffs and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

3. B — newton (N)

4. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Consumer Protection.

5. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Careers in Food and Nutrition.

6. B — Producers

7. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ventilation and Lighting 2.5 Maternal Health Care 2.6 Child Health Care 2.7 Care.

8. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Yeast Products.

9. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

10. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pastry Making.

11. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Special Treatment in Laundry Work.
